description: Mock pharmacogenomics database for gene-drug interaction checks

CYP2C19.function: Metabolizes proton pump inhibitors, antiplatelet drugs, antidepressants

conflicts.risk: Clopidogrel is a prodrug requiring CYP2C19 activation. Poor metabolizers have significantly reduced antiplatelet effect (~32% lower), substantially increasing risk of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) and stent thrombosis.
conflicts.recommendation: Avoid Clopidogrel in CYP2C19 poor metabolizers. Consider Prasugrel or Ticagrelor as alternatives. Consult cardiologist.

conflicts.risk: Omeprazole plasma levels are significantly elevated in poor metabolizers, increasing risk of side effects.
conflicts.recommendation: Reduce Omeprazole dose by 50%. Consider Pantoprazole as it has less CYP2C19 dependence.

conflicts.risk: CYP2C19 poor metabolizers have ~2-fold higher escitalopram exposure, increasing risk of QTc prolongation.
conflicts.recommendation: Initiate at 50% of the recommended dose and titrate slowly. Perform ECG monitoring.

conflicts.risk: CYP2C19 is involved in S-warfarin metabolism. Poor metabolizers may have increased warfarin exposure and bleeding risk.
conflicts.recommendation: Monitor INR closely, especially during initiation. Consider dose reduction. Use validated pharmacogenomic dosing algorithms.

conflicts.risk: Ultrarapid metabolizers clear Voriconazole too quickly, leading to subtherapeutic plasma levels and treatment failure.
conflicts.recommendation: Voriconazole is not recommended. Consider Isavuconazole or Amphotericin B.

SLCO1B1.function: Mediates hepatic uptake of statins and other drugs

conflicts.risk: SLCO1B1 *5 variant carriers have markedly elevated simvastatin acid exposure (AUC increased up to 221%), dramatically increasing risk of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis at doses ≥40mg.
conflicts.recommendation: Avoid Simvastatin doses >20mg. Switch to Rosuvastatin or Pravastatin. Monitor CK levels.

conflicts.risk: Mild increase (~1.4-fold) in atorvastatin exposure. Clinical significance is lower than with simvastatin.
conflicts.recommendation: May continue Atorvastatin with routine monitoring of muscle symptoms. Avoid high doses (>40mg).

conflicts.risk: SLCO1B1 deficiency increases repaglinide plasma concentrations, raising risk of hypoglycemia.
conflicts.recommendation: Use with caution. Monitor blood glucose more frequently. Consider dose reduction.

conflicts.risk: Some evidence of modestly increased metformin exposure with SLCO1B1 variants. Generally not clinically significant at standard doses.
conflicts.recommendation: Continue standard dosing. Monitor renal function as usual.

CYP2D6.function: Metabolizes ~25% of commonly prescribed drugs including opioids, antidepressants, antipsychotics, beta-blockers

conflicts.risk: Intermediate metabolizers have reduced conversion of codeine to morphine (~50% of normal), leading to reduced analgesic efficacy.
conflicts.recommendation: Use alternative analgesics. If opioids needed, consider morphine directly.

conflicts.risk: CYP2D6 intermediate metabolizers produce reduced levels of endoxifen (active metabolite), potentially reducing tamoxifen efficacy in breast cancer treatment.
conflicts.recommendation: Consider Aromatase Inhibitor therapy as alternative for postmenopausal patients. Discuss with oncologist.

conflicts.risk: Mildly elevated metoprolol levels may occur. Generally well tolerated in intermediate metabolizers.
conflicts.recommendation: Monitor blood pressure and heart rate. Adjust dose if bradycardia or hypotension occurs.

conflicts.risk: Poor metabolizers have severely diminished conversion to active M1 opioid metabolite, resulting in treatment failure for pain management.
conflicts.recommendation: Tramadol is not recommended. Use non-CYP2D6-dependent analgesics.

conflicts.risk: CYP2D6 poor metabolizers have 10-fold higher atomoxetine exposure, significantly increasing cardiovascular and psychiatric adverse effects.
conflicts.recommendation: Initiate at the lowest dose and titrate very slowly. Perform baseline cardiac evaluation.

conflicts.risk: Intermediate TPMT activity leads to excessive accumulation of cytotoxic thioguanine nucleotides, causing severe, life-threatening myelosuppression (bone marrow failure).
conflicts.recommendation: Reduce Azathioprine dose by 30-70%. Close monitoring of CBC every 2 weeks for first 3 months.

conflicts.risk: Intermediate TPMT activity results in toxic thiopurine accumulation and myelosuppression risk.
conflicts.recommendation: Reduce Mercaptopurine starting dose to 30-70% of standard. Weekly CBC monitoring mandatory.

conflicts.risk: Elevated thioguanine nucleotide levels with intermediate TPMT. Risk of hepatotoxicity in addition to myelosuppression.
conflicts.recommendation: Start at 50% of standard dose. Monitor liver function and CBC regularly.
